REPUBLIC OF KENYA
IN THE TAX APPEALS TRIBUNAL AT NAIROBI
TAX APPEAL NO. E1102 OF 2025
BETWEEN
UJENZI BORA CONTRACTORS LIMITED ........ APPELLANT
AND
COMMISSIONER OF DOMESTIC TAXES ........ RESPONDENT
JUDGMENT
Coram: E. N. Mutua-Chelagat (Chairperson), J. K. Lusweti, M. A. Haji (Members)
Delivered on 24th September 2026
1. The Appellant, a building contractor with 146 employees, appeals against an assessment of KES 3,846,220 in unpaid Affordable Housing Levy, penalties and interest for the period April 2024 to March 2025.
2. The Levy is imposed by section 4 of the Affordable Housing Act, 2024 on both employers and employees. The consequences of default are provided in section 7 of that Act.
3. The Appellant argues that 61 of its workers were casual labourers engaged through a labour contractor, Kazi Haraka Agencies, and that the Levy for those workers was the responsibility of that contractor.
4. The Respondent relies on muster rolls showing that the Appellant's site managers supervised and paid the workers directly, and argues that the Appellant was their employer in substance.
5. Having examined the muster rolls, the payment vouchers and the labour supply agreement, the Tribunal finds that the Appellant controlled the work, set the hours and paid the wages. The Appellant was the employer for the purposes of the Levy.
6. However, the Respondent computed penalties from April 2024 even though the Appellant's obligations in respect of the casual workers only became clear after the Respondent's public notice of 18th June 2024. Penalties for the period before that notice are not justified, given the duty of fairness under Article 47 of the Constitution.
7. The appeal is partly allowed. The principal Levy of KES 2,915,400 is upheld. The Respondent shall recompute penalties and interest from 18th June 2024 and issue an amended assessment within 30 days.
8. Each party shall bear its own costs.
E. N. MUTUA-CHELAGAT
CHAIRPERSON
